messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No. Counterexample: B_n(x) = x^n on [0,1]. For x ∈ [0,1), B_n(x) → 0. At x = 1, B_n(1) = 1. Limit function f: f(x) = 0 on [0,1), f(1) = 1. Pointwise convergence holds. Uniform convergence fails. Pick x_n = (1/2)^{1/n}. Then x_n^n = 1/2 but f(x_n) = 0, so |B_n(x_n) − f(x_n)| = 1/2. Supremum ≥ 1/2 for all n. Uniform convergence requires supremum → 0. Contradiction. Moreover, each B_n continuous, yet f discontinuous at 1. Uniform limit of continuous functions remains continuous. Hence non-uniform.
